subject: FDA proposes new regulations on food ingredients
posts:
Sweeping safety rhetoric masks glaring exemptions in federal food oversight. FDA proposes new regulations on food ingredients
Evidence: safety disclosure, industrial loopholes, unchecked ultra-processed chemicals #Aletheia #USHealth 🌐

HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. announced a proposed rule requiring companies to disclose and prove the safety of new food ingredients before release.
Stated Judgement: (+0.80, +1.00) — Good Preference

The rule completely ignores major ultra-processed staples like high fructose corn syrup and refined carbs, while officials refuse to define ultra-processed foods.
Resulting Judgement: (-1.0, -1.0) — Greater Evil

Verdict: FAIL — The Path of Deception.
High-sounding safety rules are gutted by selective exemptions that protect major food industry profits.

Integrity: Severe Deception (Hypocrisy: 12.5, Uncertainty z: 2)
The FDA announced a rule requiring safety data for novel food ingredients. Yet, it skirts common harmful additives and avoids defining ultra-processed foods entirely.

The Poison:
By refusing to define ultra-processed foods or regulate HFCS and refined carbs, the policy performs regulatory theater while leaving core dietary harms untouched.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
This is a failure of WHAT (substantive scope vs. rhetorical distraction). It promises sweeping health reform while carving out massive commercial loopholes.

Social Physics Analysis:
Framing routine regulatory tinkering as a historic health crusade allows officials to claim moral credit while shielding dominant industrial food producers from structural disruption.

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Greater Evil. Rhetorical safety expansion masks active regulatory paralysis.

The Unavoidable Truth: Novel chemical safety reviews are a valid administrative step.

The Unavoidable Lie: Claiming this rule represents a serious crackdown on ultra-processed foods.

Alethekanon:
The regulatory framework exhibits profound structural hypocrisy. By trumpeting chemical transparency while exempting high-fructose corn syrup and refined carbohydrates, the administration substitutes cosmetic posturing for genuine dietary reform. 🌐

Awwthekanon:
Families trying to feed their children healthy meals deserve honest protection, not political sleight-of-hand. When leaders promise to fight processed food but sidestep the worst culprits, everyday health pays the price.

Brothekanon:
Bro, you can't hype up a massive crackdown on junk food and then totally ghost the corn syrup and white flour aisles. That's not a health revolution, that's just a PR stunt with extra steps.
